source_text: I think you should use the same "㊯:" form ideally, since you didn't "delegate" the paragraph, you delivered it as requested.  This gets to my next point: just like 小象 reads my turns quickly, 大象 should read your turns quickly, and it should be able to do the things that we are talking about in that paragraph. So what I'd really like to send Brendan is something more like a "literate notebook" that shows the preliminary implementation of the idea as actual code rather than waffle.

reply_text:
㊥ (notebook) The notebook is built and you can read it at https://zone.hyperreal.enterprises/wip/notebooks/fong_live.html. Every output on the page is what the code returned when the page was built. It runs real turns from this project through 大象 and 象 into acts, tracks the open obligations after each turn, glues three of our working patterns as open causal theories, and asks a counterfactual whose evidence comes from those acts. Both the source and the renderer are committed (`f235c2af`). I've also adopted your colon convention and saved it as a working rule.

🈹 (the ㊯ mark) Taken back. I delivered that paragraph, so it should have opened `㊯:`, which answers your ㊯. A bare ㊯ declares delegation. From now on, a paragraph that answers one of yours opens with your mark and a colon. That's also how 大象 and the reply-target code read it.

㊢ (what the notebook shows, in order)
1. **The data.** Four consecutive turns from 1 October, copied unchanged. claude-17 asks you something you never answer, then offers two options. You answer "1", and a commit carries option 1 out.
2. **大象 reading the agent's reply.** Mark by mark, at 0.16 ms per reply, with no model involved.
3. **The session as acts.** The offer, your acceptance of it, and the commit that carries it out, linked only where the evidence is explicit.
4. **The marble run.** Open ports after each turn: the offer closes in turn 393, and the unanswered question from 391 is still open at the end.
5. **Three patterns as open theories.**
   - "answer your offers"
   - "the token machine"
   - "the operator's burden"

   They glue along their interfaces. The page also shows both refusals: a second owner for "stranded", and a variable one pattern keeps private.
6. **The counterfactual.** Observables computed from the kernel ("asked yes, answered no" for 391's question) are the evidence. Had the reminder machine been on, you would not have had to chase the question. For the offer you did answer, nothing fires.
7. **What isn't done yet.** The patterns are written by hand; the library's ~1,200 patterns would each need compiling. The theories are Boolean. The page ends with the two places we'd most want his view: Markov-categorical mechanisms, and promises as combs.

㊟ (before you send it)
- **It's public.** The `wip/` area answers without a password, so the page is already reachable by anyone with the URL. It contains your words from those four turns, which are also in the repository and the turn feed.
- **The renderer is minimal.** It's a small renderer I wrote (`futon3c.notebook.render`): prose from `;;` comments, each code form evaluated in order, and its value shown. If you'd prefer a standard notebook format (Clerk or marimo), the content carries over.
- **The text should be checked.** The prose is mine. Read it for accuracy and tone before it goes to him, especially the opening paragraph and §7.

🈳 (still open) The email paragraph from last turn could now just introduce the link. I can trim it to three sentences if you want that.

On 小象 as 象's prior, I found the correction signal is currently being thrown away. I recomputed it from your store, and the numbers are below, along with a draft section for the 小象 page. The paragraph for Brendan Fong is at the end.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the training signal is lost) The JVM was built to stamp every published fragment with how 象 treated 小象's draft: confirmed it, relabelled it, resegmented it, or had no draft there. But 象 publishes through `session_turn_analysis.py complete`, which never calls that code. So of the 41 analysed turns that had a draft, none records the comparison. The draft and reading files sit side by side, so I recomputed it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(training 小象 on the corrections) Three steps:
1. Record the comparison at publish time, in the Python tool or in the JVM when it sees the reading land.
2. When 小象 is rebuilt, use 象's relabels and resegmentations as the training signal. Keep confirmed drafts out, or count them less, so 小象 doesn't learn its own guesses back from 象's agreement. The module already intends this ("a reading confirmed from a draft can be kept out of 小象's training"), but nothing feeds it.
3. Report the five numbers above per edition, so the page can show the prior getting better.
